_comment: F-16A Block 10/15 Level-1 inputs (type/statistical). Read by F16GeomL1, F16AeroL1, F16PropL1, F16WeightsL1. Full docs: F16GeomL1.md, AeroL1.md, F16PropL1.md, F16WeightsL1.md, docs/*_parameter_usage.md; open items in VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md.
_cite: Main!/Wt! = Brandt-F16-A.xls tabs; TO = T.O. 1F-16A-1; Raymer = Raymer 6th ed.; Mattingly = Mattingly: Aircraft Engine Design, 2nd edition; todo = VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md.
_aircraft_category_src: ONE canonical class flag for every discipline. Selects Roskam I Tbl 3.5 (S_wet) / Raymer Tbl 6.3 (L_fus) / Raymer 7th Tbl 4.1 (AR_eq) / Raymer Tbl 3.1 + Roskam I Tbl 2.15 (empty weight) / Roskam I Tbl 3.1 (CLmax) / Raymer Tbl 12.3 (Cfe) rows. Those tables name their categories differently (Roskam's CLmax table says 'fighter'), so each lookup translates this canonical value to its own table's row name -- see AeroL1.to_CLmax_table_row. Do NOT rename a table row to match this key: the row name is what the textbook prints.

geometry._note: ★ NO INPUTS AT L1. M_max = 2.0 was DELETED here (Phase 4, 2026-07-25): it was the THIRD copy of the design max Mach, which now lives once in examples/F16A/f16a_requirements.json as design_mach [Brandt Main! aircraft.Mmax; GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json:9]. It is still CONSUMED -- F16GeomL1 feeds it to GeomL1.get_AR_eq (Raymer 7th Tbl 4.1, GeomL1.m:121-129) -- so this is a consolidation, not a removal. The repoint has LANDED: F16GeomL1(json_path, req_path) reads design_mach from the requirements file. todo 2026-07-25 Phase 4 §P4-14.

aerodynamics._src: design_type [Mattingly Sec. 2.3.1: uncambered -> K2=0]; curve [Mattingly Fig. 2.10 CD0 technology array]; AR/Lambda_LE_deg [real F-16 wing spec, same values as f16a_L2.json .geometry.wing -- Brandt Main! tab -- feeding AeroL1.k1_from_geometry (Raymer Eq. 12.48-12.50/12.51), NOT a curve table -- see F16AeroL1.m class header]

cd0_curve._src: [Mattingly Fig. 2.10 CD0(M) fighter] via 5 AAF worked points (mattingly_data.md PART 9); Future = copy of Current

propulsion._src: engine_type [F100-PW-200 class; selects PropL1 lapse m=0.6 (Martins metabook Eq. 10.9) + TSFC rows (Raymer Tbl 3.3)]; T_SL AB SLS lbf [Engn(s)!T_AB_SLS = Main!D29; TO Sec. I]. T_SL_wet is NOT an input: it is Dependent on T_SL (same quantity, AB name).

weights._src: W_payload_fixed [Wt tab: crew + fixed equipment]; W_payload_expendable [Wt tab: stores]. Regression coefficients are aircraft_category-selected toolbox Constants (Raymer Tbl 3.1 / Roskam I Tbl 2.15); edition/table drift: todo 2026-07-24 §3c. W_energy is NOT an input: internal fuel is a mission-analysis OUTPUT (Brandt Wt!B6 = W_TO - payload - OEW is back-calculated), set by the sizing loop.

subsystems._note: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED -- no F16SubsystemsL1 class exists yet (docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md, Casey-approved, scribe-complete 2026-07-31; io pass 2026-07-31). Tabulation-only inputs, no geometry (Nicolai & Carichner Ch. 8 style). Fuel-packaging-factor table (subplan item 1) is NOT usable at L1 (no geometric raw volume exists yet) -- it first applies at L2, see f16a_L2.json .subsystems.fuel.packaging_factor. No landing-gear block at L1 by design (subplan Fidelity split: a bay-volume estimate needs a fuselage envelope, which doesn't exist before GeomL2).

fuel._cite_fuel: [Nicolai & Carichner, Table 8.6, p.210] JP-4 = 6.5 lb/gal (48.6 lb/ft3); docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §2. T.O. 1F-16A-1 certifies the F-16 for JP-4/JP-5/JP-8 (temp_AI/docs/disciplines/reference_extracts/usaf_f16_data.md:87, 'Fuels: JP-4 / JP-5 / JP-8'), so JP-4 is chosen here as this example's single active fuel type, not because JP-5/JP-8 are inapplicable to the airframe. The fuel-type -> density LOOKUP TABLE itself (JP-4 6.5 / JP-5 6.8 / JP-8 6.7 / Aviation gas 6.0 lb/gal) is a Nicolai Table 8.6 published constant and belongs in the future SubsystemsL1 toolbox code as a Constant, not duplicated here -- same JSON/code split as AeroL1.CLmax_table (only the selector, aircraft_category, lives in JSON; the full table lives in code).

avionics._aircraft_category_table_row_note: Translates the top-level aircraft_category='jet_fighter' flag to [Raymer 6th ed., Ch. 11, Table 11.6 'Avionics Weights,' p.375]'s own printed row name 'Fighters' (range 0.03-0.08 of W_empty) -- same category-to-row-name translation pattern as AeroL1.to_CLmax_table_row; do not rename this row to match the top-level key. The full 8-row table belongs in the future SubsystemsL1 toolbox code, not duplicated here.
avionics._cite_weight_fraction: [Raymer 6th ed., Ch. 11, Table 11.6, p.375] Fighters row = 0.03-0.08 x W_empty (docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §3). 0.055 = range midpoint -- an EXPLICIT JUDGMENT CALL flagged for sign-off: the subplan states picking a point in this range is 'an implementation-time choice, not a citation gap' and names two options -- midpoint ~=0.055 (used here) or the legacy code's 0.03 (the low end of the same correct range, not a wrong value). Change to 0.03 if the low end is preferred.
avionics._cite_density_lb_per_ft3: [Raymer 6th ed., Ch. 11, p.375, prose immediately after Table 11.6]: 'volume can be estimated assuming that avionics has an average density of about 30-45 lb/ft3.' 37.5 = range midpoint. DECIDED fidelity split (Casey, 2026-07-31; docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §4): L1 stays on Raymer end-to-end (fraction + density from the same Table 11.6 page, no geometry needed); L2/L3 switch to Nicolai's flat 45 lb/ft3 -- see f16a_L2.json .subsystems.avionics.
